title: If Only: Wishes About the Past

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *ojalá* with the pluperfect subjunctive from B2 Unit 16: *Ojalá hubiera estudiado más*, "I wish I had studied more". It is a wish about something that did not happen, so it can no longer come true. People who live far from home use it often, and so does anyone who thinks back on a decision.

sections.title: Ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive
rows: Ojalá hubiera podido quedarme con mi familia.
I wish I had been able to stay with my family.
I wish we had taken more flour.
Ojalá no hubieras tenido que irte.
I wish you had not had to leave.
If only I had been able to come back earlier!

items.spanish: Ojalá hubiera podido quedarme con mi familia.
items.english: I wish I had been able to stay with my family.
I wish we had taken more flour.
I wish I had left earlier.
If only I had been able to come back earlier!

sections.content: Use *hubiera* (or *hubiese*), never *habría*, after *ojalá*: *Ojalá hubiera venido*, not *Ojalá habría venido*. A wish about the past is always a regret. These sentences express a feeling: they do not say what really happened.
